scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

identityAssessment.finding: The imported 1492 to 1500 polygon lies in the Pudding River and French Prairie vicinity, about 123.11 to 122.59 degrees west and 44.91 to 45.37 degrees north. The intended Ahantchuyuk identity is consistent, but the polygon is not an independently verified territorial survey.

scopeNotes: Regional Kalapuya food practices and present Grand Ronde programs are explicitly labelled; neither is automatically attributed to every historical Ahantchuyuk household.
The OHS catalogue identifies the French Prairie band and supplies page locators. The manuscript images themselves were not inspected; no individual names, quantities or transcriptions are invented.
The log book’s combined census total covers several peoples, not just Ahantchuyuk.
The treaty was negotiated through several January 1855 assent dates. The card uses the year rather than presenting one day as every community’s signing date.
The precise Ahantchuyuk signatory mapping is not inferred from similar spellings such as Chafan, Chapen or Calapooia.
The source’s uncertain population estimates, speculation about particular mission children and unsupported nutritional percentages are not repeated.
Neither the 1861 flood that destroyed the settler town nor the 1954 federal termination is a date for the people’s extinction.
No ancient date is invented for undated ethnographic practices. No verified Grand Ronde map destination is available for a successor navigation link.
